claim: KBRA assigned a long-term rating of AA with Stable Outlook to the Cities of Dallas and Fort Worth 2025A-1 (AMT), 2025A-2 (AMT), and 2025B (Non-AMT) Joint Revenue Refunding and Improvement Bonds issued on behalf of DFW.
source_title: KBRA Assigns AA Rating, Stable Outlook to the Cities of Dallas and Fort Worth, TX Airport Joint Revenue Refunding and Improvement Bonds
supporting_excerpt: KBRA assigns a long-term rating of AA to the Joint Revenue Refunding and Improvement Bonds Series 2025A-1 (AMT), Joint Revenue Refunding and Improvement Bonds Series 2025A-2 (AMT), and Joint Revenue Refunding and Improvement Bonds Series 2025B (Non-AMT) issued by the Cities of Dallas and Fort Worth, TX on behalf of Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW). The Outlook is Stable.
caveat: KBRA rating; Moody's, S&P, and Fitch letters on prior series may differ and should be cited separately.

claim: On May 1, 2025 DFW and American Airlines announced the acceleration and expansion of Terminal F to approximately 31 gates and ~$4 billion, and extended the Use and Lease Agreement between DFW and American to 2043.
source_title: DFW Airport and American Airlines Announce Acceleration and Expansion of Plans for Terminal F
supporting_excerpt: The new plan extends the Use and Lease Agreement between DFW and American to 2043 and increases the estimated Terminal F investment to about $4 billion.
caveat: Scope was originally announced in 2023 as a 15-gate, ~$1.6B facility under a 10-year U&L; the 2025 announcement is the acceleration/expansion.

claim: The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (PL 118-63) is a five-year, $105.5 billion package including $19.4 billion for airport infrastructure improvement grants and left the Passenger Facility Charge cap unchanged at $4.50.
source_title: H.R.3935 - FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (118th Congress)
supporting_excerpt: FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 - reauthorizes FAA programs through FY2028; funding lines include operations, facilities and equipment, airport infrastructure grants, and research and development.
caveat: PFC cap statutorily unchanged; commercial airport sponsors continue to be permitted to charge up to $4.50 per boarded passenger per segment.

claim: Chris McLaughlin was appointed CEO of DFW by unanimous vote of the DFW Airport Board of Directors, assuming the role on May 19, 2025, succeeding retiring CEO Sean Donohue.
source_title: DFW Airport Board Appoints Chris McLaughlin New CEO Following Global Executive Search
supporting_excerpt: Mr. McLaughlin will assume the role on May 19, succeeding current CEO Sean Donohue, who is retiring after more than a decade leading DFW. Mr. McLaughlin's appointment was made official by a unanimous vote of the DFW Airport Board of Directors.
caveat: McLaughlin was previously DFW EVP of Operations from 2021; prior COO at Denver International Airport; former TSA Office of Security Operations, where PreCheck was established.

claim: The DFW Airport Board of Directors is composed of 12 members: 11 voting seats (7 appointed by the City of Dallas, 4 by the City of Fort Worth in proportion to ownership) and one non-voting seat that rotates annually among Irving, Grapevine, Euless, and Coppell.
supporting_excerpt: DFW Airport's Board of Directors is composed of 12 members, 11 of whom are appointed by the city councils of the Airport's owner cities. Seven represent the City of Dallas and four represent the City of Fort Worth, in accordance with each city's ownership interest in the Airport. In order to facilitate communication between and among the Airport and its neighbors, a 12th, non-voting board position representing one of the Airport's four neighboring cities -- Irving, Grapevine, Euless and Coppell -- is filled on an annual, rotating basis.
caveat: Term length is set by ordinance rather than statute; DFW Airport Board is historically exempted (via Ordinance No. 9272) from standard nine-member/term-limit provisions applied to other Dallas boards.

claim: DFW sets airline rates under a uniform Use and Lease Agreement with a base term October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2033; an April 2025 offer letter gives each signatory the option, exercisable through September 30, 2033, to extend the term to September 30, 2043.
supporting_excerpt: DFW sets airline rates under a uniform Use and Lease Agreement between the Dallas Fort Worth International Airport Board and each Air Carrier with a base term October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2033. An April 2025 offer letter gives each Signatory Airline the option, exercisable through September 30, 2033, to extend to September 30, 2043.
caveat: Secondary source summarizing primary DFW disclosures; confirm directly against the executed U&L and April 2025 offer letter in the DFW bond disclosure package before citing in an executed document.

claim: DFW is classified as a hybrid-residual airport for airline ratemaking purposes.
source_title: Airline Rate Methodologies: Residual vs Compensatory (DWU Consulting)
supporting_excerpt: Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW) is classified as a hybrid residual airport, which means it uses a hybrid residual approach to setting airline costs.
caveat: Secondary analyst characterization; the operative rate methodology is defined inside the U&L itself.

claim: Moody's Aa3+ US airport medians reported approximately 72 days cash on hand in 2024.
source_title: Airport Bond Ratings: Fitch, Moody's, S&P DSCR (DWU Consulting)
supporting_excerpt: Moody's Aa3+ airports averaged 72 days cash on hand (2024 medians) per Moody's Airport Monitor.
denominator: US airports rated Aa3 or higher by Moody's
caveat: Secondary source citing Moody's Airport Monitor; verify directly in the Moody's Airport Monitor publication before external citation.

claim: Fitch's US airport methodology sorts single-carrier hubs into concentration bands of approximately <30%, 30–60%, and >60%; Moody's carrier-base subfactor scores concentration around the ~50% level as a weaker credit factor.
source_title: Airport Bond Ratings: Fitch, Moody's, S&P DSCR (DWU Consulting)
supporting_excerpt: Fitch's Transportation Infrastructure Rating Criteria groups airports at ~30%, 30–60%, and >60% single-carrier shares, while Moody's scorecards include a Carrier Base subfactor (Primary Carrier as % of Total Enplanements) with weaker scores around the ~50% level.
caveat: Secondary source paraphrasing Fitch and Moody's methodologies; the original Fitch Transportation Infrastructure Rating Criteria (updated January 2025) and Moody's Global Rating Methodology for U.S. Airports (February 2023) are the primary references.

claim: In July 2024 Fitch affirmed CVG (Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport) at A+ / Stable, citing Delta de-hubbing completion (~35% of CVG passengers) and DSCR of 11.6x.
source_title: Airport Bond Ratings: Fitch, Moody's, S&P DSCR (DWU Consulting)
supporting_excerpt: Fitch affirmed CVG at A+ (Stable) in July 2024, citing Delta's de-hubbing completion (~35% of CVG passengers) and DSCR improvement to 11.6x.
denominator: airport gross revenues to senior debt service
caveat: Secondary source; verify against the underlying Fitch rating action release before citing in an executed document.

claim: The CBP Reimbursable Services Program was established under the Cross-Border Trade Enhancement Act of 2016 and enables CBP to collaborate with private-sector and government entities to provide additional inspection services on a reimbursable basis; the program has grown to include participation by 375 private-sector entities and state and local governments.
source_title: Reimbursable Services Program - U.S. Customs and Border Protection
supporting_excerpt: The Reimbursable Services Program has grown since it began in 2013 to include participation by 375 private sector entities and state and local governments. Under the reimbursable services agreement, mandatory services such as customs, agricultural processing, border security services, immigration inspections and support services at ports of entry can be expanded.
caveat: Reimbursable services at airports with 100,000+ annual arriving international passengers are limited to overtime and support costs; at smaller airports Section 481 authority allows reimbursement of salaries and benefits of up to 5 full-time officers.

claim: Approximately 60% of DFW's passenger traffic is connecting.
source_title: American Airlines Terminals at DFW: Full 2026 Guide (secondary reporting summarizing DFW connecting share)
supporting_excerpt: About 60% of DFW's passenger traffic consists of connecting passengers.
caveat: Secondary source. The run prompt separately asserts 'two-thirds of American's DFW customers connect,' which is a carrier-level statistic distinct from the airport-level ~60%. Airport-level and carrier-level connecting shares should be cited separately; primary DFW and American traffic statistics should be verified before citing in an executed document.
